newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: INTERVIEW - Lusotur sees profits in 1997.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Lusotur sees profits in 1997.

text.p: Loss-making Portuguese leisure group Lusotur, which is building Europe's biggest residential tourism complex in the Algarve, expects to return to profit in 1997, its president Andre Jordan said.

"We expect to be in profit in 1997 and to have a dramatic increase in profits in 1998 and 1999," the 63-year-old Brazilian entrepreneur told Reuters in an interview late on Thursday. He gave no figures.
"We will have a good product and we expect to see continuous signs of recovery in the property market in the Algarve," the Polish-born businessman said.
Lusotur posted a first half consolidated net loss of 436 million escudos ($2.8 million) in 1996, compared with a loss of 331 million escudos ($2.1 million) in the first half of 1995.
Teresa Ferreira de Lima, controller of Jordan's holding company Cofipsa SGPS, said she expected Lusotur to post a loss for the full year in 1996.
Jordan said the reason for Lusotur's losses was that the company still had "little commercial product to sell."

Lusotur was focusing its energies on expanding a vast tourism complex in Vilamoura, 20 km (15 miles) from Faro, in the Algarve region of southern Portugal, and would boost sales of residential real estate next year, he said.

The 100 billion escudo ($644 million) Vilamoura XXI project, scheduled to be completed 10 years from now, will offer residential real estate and entertainment facilities over a landscaped area of 850 hectares (2,100 acres), Jordan said.

"It will be the biggest tourism complex in Europe," he said. "Vilamoura already has 35,000 beds -- more than the island of Madeira," he said. "When it is completed, it will be bigger than Monte Carlo."
The project will add 25,000 beds to the existing Vilamoura complex as well as a shopping and health centre, 18-hole golf course, cinemas, discos, bowling and horse-riding facilities.
Jordan said the complex would be environmentally friendly and "low-rise". No building would be more than four floors high.
Lusotur expects to finance the Vilamoura XXI project by raising capital, taking on debt and forming joint ventures.

"We will probably increase capital, we will probably take on debt and we will probably associate with third parties in parts of the development," Jordan said. "We have ongoing discussions with major international investors."
The financing arrangements for Vilamoura XXI should be agreed by mid-1997, Jordan said. Lusotur has low debt now.
The Vilamoura complex was aimed at middle and higher income consumers, Jordan said.
"We look at ourselves as an international product, Portugal- based," he said. Lusotur has no plans to expand abroad.
Jordan's Cofipsa has large real estate interests in Portugal, including the luxury Quinta do Lago development in the Algarve and the Belas Clube de Campo residential and golf complex near Lisbon.
Lusotur shares closed at 2,500 escudos on Lisbon bourse on Thursday. ($1=155.25 escudos)
